findings.reason: The diff deletes the `node.tag !== defaultScalarTag.tagName` return, leaving only the isKey/PLAIN check at styler_defaults.ts:65. presenter.ts:417 then sets shouldPrintTag for any non-plain scalar whose tag isn't the default string tag. That goes against the documented contract at presenter.ts:99 ('Quotes all non-key strings'). No story.md is in the packet, so breaks is left out.
findings.claim: Removing the default-scalar-tag guard makes forceQuotes quote plain numbers, booleans, nulls and custom-tag scalars, and presenter.ts then adds explicit tags to them (e.g. `n: !!int '1'`).
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `if (layout.node.tag !== layout.presenterOptions.schema.defaultScalarTag.tagName) return`, so the only remaining guard is `layout.isKey || layout.style !== SCALAR_STYLE.PLAIN`. In presenter.ts:417, `shouldPrintTag = ... || (layout.style !== SCALAR_STYLE.PLAIN && node.tag !== state.defaultScalarTagName)` then adds an explicit tag to every non-string scalar that ends up quoted. This breaks the documented contract at presenter.ts:99 ('Quotes all non-key strings using quoteStyle') and the CHANGELOG entry 'forceQuotes option to force quoting non-key strings'. The rewritten comment ('applies only to plain values') shows the change of scope was deliberate, but nothing in the packet asks for it.

findings.reason: The diff changes only styler_defaults.ts. The forceQuotes test at dump-options.test.mjs:93-103 dumps only string values ({ hello: 'world' }), so it passes whether or not the tag guard is there.
